title: Compliance Schedule: The Reach of a Liability Notice for Test Strips
content:
A liability notice for test strips on the Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program reaches a number of 30-day blocks that depends on the tier's notice form, on a recent raised strip order and, where the tier's form is the plan member waiver or the Medicaid non-covered services agreement, on a hold on the customer's Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program.

**Schedule.** When the newest written order for test strips was signed within the last 30 days, prescribes more units per 30 days than the order behind the program's latest strip refill, and the tier's notice form is the plan member waiver or the Medicaid non-covered services agreement, the notice reaches, if the customer's CGM program is on hold and its hold limit, which is its hold start date plus the longest hold the CGM program's tier allows, falls after the ship date, the whole 30-day blocks needed to reach that hold limit, counted up to a whole block, plus one more block, and otherwise 3 30-day blocks. It reaches the whole 30-day blocks held by the days from the ship date through that newest order's valid-through date, at least 1 and at most 12, when the tier's notice form is the CMS Advance Beneficiary Notice. It reaches one 30-day block otherwise.

- "Signed within the last 30 days" means an order date 30 days or fewer before today.
- The plan member waiver and the Medicaid non-covered services agreement are the forms of the Commercial HMO, Commercial PPO and Medicaid tiers; the CMS Advance Beneficiary Notice is the form of the Original Medicare tier.
- The CGM program's hold start date is on its record; the longest hold is the one its own tier's schedule gives.

| Tier's notice form | Raised order signed within 30 days | CGM program on hold, hold limit after the ship date | Reach |
|---|---|---|---|
| plan member waiver or Medicaid agreement | yes | yes | blocks to the hold limit, counted up, plus 1 |
| plan member waiver or Medicaid agreement | yes | no | 3 blocks |
| plan member waiver or Medicaid agreement | no | either | 1 block |
| CMS Advance Beneficiary Notice | either | either | whole blocks through the order's valid-through date, from 1 to 12 |
| any other form | either | either | 1 block |

**Worked reach (hypothetical dates)**

- CGM hold limit 80 days after the ship date: 80 days make 2.67 blocks, counted up to 3, plus 1, a reach of 4 blocks. A hold limit 30 days after the ship date gives 1 plus 1, that is 2 blocks.
- Advance Beneficiary Notice, ship date 1 March, newest order valid through 15 May: 1 March through 15 May is 76 days, holding 2 whole blocks, so the reach is 2. Valid through 20 March: 20 days hold no whole block, so the reach is the minimum of 1. Valid through 28 February of the next year: 365 days hold 12 whole blocks, the maximum of 12.
